rationale: C13 plausibly supplied a material template for the child’s appeal for mutual-security appropriations. Both letters present foreign military assistance as inseparable from United States security, stress that allied nations bear substantial burdens themselves, explain that equipment requires long production and delivery lead times, and treat military and economic assistance as complementary parts of a unified free-world defense program. C04 is a secondary structural analogue for opposing congressional appropriation cuts, while C11 shares the mutual-security rationale but serves a different statutory determination.

shared_material.child_excerpt: This program and these appropriations directly involve the security of our own Nation. The program is specifically directed toward strengthening the collective security of the free nations-in which the safety of our Nation is inescapably involved.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The increased military aid program I am recommending is as vital to our national security as the increased military appropriations I have previously recommended for our own armed forces. The security of the United States is inseparably bound up with the survival of the free nations associated with us in the common defense.
shared_material.explanation: Both frame foreign military assistance as an integral and direct component of United States national security.

shared_material.child_excerpt: It must be remembered, however, that our funds are exceeded by much larger funds expended by our NATO and other allies themselves.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The greater share of this effort will, of course, be assumed by these nations themselves, out of their own resources. However, the serious problems with which they are confronted make it necessary for us to increase our military aid to them
shared_material.explanation: Both counter objections to American spending by emphasizing the larger defense effort undertaken by allied countries.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the lead time required in almost every case...has been a very long one. The emphasis in our program on major items of equipment, such as aircraft and ships...require a relatively large amount of lead-time financing.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The bulk of this money will be used to procure military equipment of the kind which takes a long time to produce. Much of it will not come off the production lines for 12, 18, or 24 months after the signing of the procurement contracts.
shared_material.explanation: The child reuses the concrete procurement-pipeline argument that current appropriations are necessary well before equipment can be delivered.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I wish also to emphasize the importance of economic and technical assistance...These programs...are an integral part of our program for America's security.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The expansion of the mutual defense program will not be a substitute for economic aid. On the contrary...it [is] all the more necessary to continue our economic aid.
shared_material.explanation: Both integrate nonmilitary assistance into the same overall security case rather than treating military aid as sufficient by itself.
